content: 1. The evidence was insufficient to exclude the possibility of a meaningful benefit. 2. One study included in the analysis had significant design limitations. 3. The confidence interval was wide and crossed the line of no effect, with few events reported, making it impossible to exclude the potential for either harm or benefit. 4. The comparison of internal versus external tocodynamometry during augmented labor (maternal outcomes) was assessed in a study by Bakker JJH et al., published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2013 (Issue 8, CD006947). 5. The quality of evidence for maternal outcomes was rated as moderate, with an estimated effect of 76 more events per 1,000 (ranging from 6 more to 161 more). This was considered important. 6. Another assessment showed 33 fewer events per 1,000 (ranging from 54 fewer to 12 more), but the quality of evidence was rated as very low, and the importance was deemed critical. 7. Most studies contributing data to the analysis had design limitations. 8. Some analyses reported no events, further limiting the reliability of the findings. 9. The confidence intervals in several analyses were wide, crossed the line of no effect, and were based on small sample sizes, reducing the certainty of the results. 10. The comparison of internal versus external tocodynamometry during augmented labor (infant outcomes) was also assessed in the same study by Bakker JJH et al. 11. For infant outcomes, the quality of evidence was rated as low, with an estimated effect of 60 more events per 1,000 (ranging from 19 fewer to 183 more). This was considered critical. 12. Another analysis showed 0 fewer events per 1,000 (ranging from 8 fewer to 118 more), with the quality of evidence rated as low and the importance deemed important. 13. Most studies contributing data to the infant outcomes analysis also had design limitations. 14. Some analyses reported no events, further limiting the reliability of the findings. 15. The confidence intervals in these analyses were wide, crossed the line of no effect, and were based on few events, reducing the certainty of the results. 16. One study included in the infant outcomes analysis had significant design limitations. 17.
